status: checkpoint 1 confirmed by the owner (synthetic example)
goal: Estimate the pressure at the outlet of each segment of a liquid line for a given flow rate, fluid and pipe age, and the total pressure drop of the line.

users.use: Types the flow and fluid inputs, pastes new segment data after a survey, reads the outlet pressure.
Asks the engineer whether a planned rate keeps the outlet pressure above the delivery minimum.

decisions: Can the line carry the planned flow rate with enough outlet pressure?
Which segments cause most of the pressure loss?
manualSteps: Paste the segment survey into the Segments sheet.
Pick the roughness by pipe age from the Lookups sheet (done by the VLOOKUP).
Copy the summary values into the weekly report.

B004.name: Pipe roughness
B004.meaning: Absolute roughness for the pipe age.

B016.name: Velocity
B016.meaning: Mean velocity from the volumetric flow rate.

B018.name: Friction factor
B018.meaning: Swamee-Jain approximation of the Colebrook equation.

B019.name: Friction loss
B019.meaning: Darcy-Weisbach friction loss of the segment.

B020.name: Elevation loss
B020.meaning: Hydrostatic head of the elevation change, converted to kPa.
